title: Bounded Ops alerts views
summary: Moves the protected Ops Alerts page and Alerts API off full alert-log loading and onto bounded recent-alert queries.
changes: Render /alerts from fetch_recent_alerts with the requested Ops limit instead of reversing the full alert log.
Return /api/alerts from the same bounded recent-alert query path.
Add regression coverage that protected Ops alert views do not call the full alert-log fetch path.
security_notes: The protected Ops alert surface remains read-only and behind the existing Ops authentication dependency.
The change reduces observer-surface load from large alert logs without altering HMI, Modbus, bind hosts, ports or authentication.

title: SQL-backed Ops sources page
summary: Moves the protected Ops Sources page off full event-log loading and onto bounded SQLite source-activity aggregates.
changes: Add a bounded fetch_source_activity query for source counts, sessions, first/last seen values and top activity fields.
Render /sources from SQL-backed source activity rows instead of materializing every raw event JSON record.
Add regression coverage that the Sources page does not call the full event-log fetch path.
security_notes: Source sorting remains allowlisted and does not introduce request-controlled SQL fragments.
The change is limited to the protected Ops backend and does not alter HMI, Modbus, bind hosts, ports or authentication.

title: Package version metadata sync
summary: Synchronizes Python package metadata with the protected backend version history so Docker builds no longer report stale package versions.
changes: Update pyproject.toml and uv.lock package metadata to 1.4.17.
Update honeypot.__version__ to 1.4.17.
Add regression coverage that package metadata, lockfile metadata and the backend version history stay aligned.
security_notes: The change is metadata-only and does not alter attacker-facing HMI, Modbus behavior, Ops authentication, bind hosts or ports.
Keeping shipped package metadata aligned with the protected Ops version log reduces operator confusion during deployment verification.

title: Protected versions API
summary: Adds a protected JSON endpoint for the backend version log so operators and deployment automation can verify the shipped backend without scraping HTML.
changes: Expose the backend version log at /api/versions behind the existing Ops authentication dependency.
Return latest version metadata, total version count and structured version rows for automation-friendly checks.
Cover the endpoint with integration tests, including route-specific Basic Auth enforcement.
security_notes: The API is read-only, hidden from OpenAPI output and available only through the protected Ops backend surface.
The payload contains release metadata only and does not expose host paths, secrets, credentials or attacker-facing debug detail.

title: Ops-managed Modbus timing defaults
summary: Moves the bounded Modbus response timing profile into protected Ops settings while keeping .env values as a boot fallback.
changes: Add Modbus timing controls to Ops Settings with 0..2000 ms validation and min/max ordering.
Let the Modbus server read timing bounds from Ops settings at response time, falling back to .env when no Ops value exists.
Document the configuration boundary so boot-only and security-critical values remain in .env.
security_notes: Ops-managed timing is bounded and does not alter bind hosts, ports, ingress approvals, or exposed routes.
Deployment-critical, boot-time, evidence-path and egress settings remain outside the runtime UI.

title: Rare historical maintenance windows
summary: Adds a rare planned-maintenance marker to generated plant history so trend data contains a bounded operational interruption without a live maintenance scheduler.
changes: Persist operating_mode on plant history samples with a backward-compatible SQLite migration.
Seed at most one short deterministic pseudo-random maintenance window in fresh 30-day generation history.
Surface historical maintenance context on the existing HMI trends page.
security_notes: The feature does not add attacker-facing routes, public ports, peer traffic, or a live runtime scheduler.
Maintenance realism stays bounded to generated historical data and avoids real plant schedules or OEM-specific behavior.

title: Bounded Modbus response timing
summary: Adds an optional bounded Modbus response timing profile so exposed protocol replies can look less perfectly instantaneous while keeping safe defaults.
changes: Add validated MODBUS_RESPONSE_DELAY_MIN_MS and MODBUS_RESPONSE_DELAY_MAX_MS settings with disabled 0/0 defaults.
Apply deterministic bounded response delays before Modbus ADUs are sent.
Cover the timing profile with contract tests that use an injected delay callback instead of wall-clock assertions.
security_notes: The timing profile is bounded to 0..2000 milliseconds and refuses min values above max values.
The feature does not create background peer traffic or broaden the exposed protocol surface.

title: Fictional Modbus identity profile
summary: Replaces generic Modbus identity values with an internally consistent fictional device profile that looks operational without cloning a real OEM.
changes: Expose fictional device-class, family, model, hardware, firmware, serial and capability values in the Modbus identity block.
Update Modbus unit, contract and runtime assertions to the new identity profile.
Document the identity block and no-OEM rule in the register matrix.
security_notes: Identity values avoid real manufacturer names, order-code schemes, firmware strings, module IDs, MAC/OUI values and exact OEM register maps.
The exposed-research sweep validates the fictional PPC identity without depending on a real vendor fingerprint.

title: Modbus fingerprint contract QA
summary: Adds contract coverage for Modbus fingerprint realism so protocol behavior, identity consistency and quiet exception paths remain intentional.
changes: Add fingerprint contract tests for the intentional function-code matrix.
Verify identity-block consistency across active Modbus units.
Assert write-readback process effects and quiet Modbus exceptions for unknown units or gaps.
security_notes: The tests reduce accidental emulator tells such as overbroad function-code support or unrealistic write behavior.
Rejected protocol paths remain observable in Ops events without exposing attacker-facing debug detail.

title: Attacker-facing leakage gate
summary: Adds a repository hardening gate for attacker-facing content and documents the no-background-network realism decision.
changes: Scan attacker-facing templates and locale files for private path leaks, debug/framework fingerprints, real vendor clone terms and deployable-looking secrets.
Keep public documentation under the absolute-path leak check.
Document that background peer traffic is not simulated for realism; HMI and Modbus remain the intended exposed surfaces.
security_notes: The gate helps prevent accidental disclosure of host paths, framework internals, real OEM clone terms or secret-looking material.
Avoiding fake background peer traffic keeps the honeypot's attack surface bounded and auditable.

title: SQL-backed Ops dashboard
summary: Moves the protected Ops dashboard summary, recent activity, recent alerts and top-source rows onto bounded SQLite queries so the page no longer materializes the full event and alert logs.
changes: Use SQL aggregate queries for dashboard totals and active-alert counts.
Fetch only bounded recent event and alert rows for dashboard tables.
Build dashboard top sources from grouped SQLite activity records.
security_notes: Dashboard data remains read-only and available only through the protected Ops backend path.
The new aggregation queries use static SQL with no request-controlled fragments.

title: Paged Ops events view
summary: Moves the protected Ops Events view to SQL-backed pages and adds a next-100 navigation action for reviewing older activity without loading the full event log.
changes: Fetch only the requested Events page plus one sentinel row from SQLite.
Add a Show next 100 events action that keeps the active filters.
Apply the same paged query path to the Events API and filtered CSV export.
security_notes: Event filters stay parameterized and the new cursor parameter is range-validated by FastAPI.
The Events view remains available only through the protected Ops backend path.

title: Multi-source Ops event filters
summary: Extends the Ops Events source-IP filter to support multiple included and !-excluded IP tokens with matching CSV export behavior.
changes: Allow multiple source_ip tokens separated by spaces or commas.
Treat !IP tokens as source exclusions and AND as a readability separator.
Apply the same include/exclude semantics to filtered Events CSV exports.
security_notes: Filtering remains in server-side allowlisted application logic and does not introduce raw SQL fragments.
CSV exports remain protected by the Ops backend authentication path and keep formula-prefix neutralization.

title: Dashboard top sources by event volume
summary: Sorts the protected Ops dashboard Top Sources table by event count so the busiest sources stand out immediately.
changes: Use events-desc ordering for the dashboard Top Sources table.
Keep the detailed Sources page sort controls unchanged.
Add regression coverage for dashboard source ordering.
security_notes: The change is read-only presentation logic in the protected Ops backend.
No event data, source-IP handling or public honeypot surface is changed.

title: Filtered Ops events CSV export
summary: Adds a protected CSV export for the current Ops Events filter view so operators can analyze source-specific activity offline.
changes: Add an Export filtered CSV action to the Ops Events page.
Reuse the existing event_type, source_ip, result and limit filters for /events/export.csv.
Export stable event columns including timestamp, source, action, result, endpoint, message and requested value.
security_notes: The CSV export is available only through the protected Ops backend.
Spreadsheet-formula prefixes in exported cells are neutralized before streaming the CSV.

title: Highlighted Ops control attempts
summary: Highlights HMI control and switching attempts in the protected Ops events table so human interaction stands out during source investigation.
changes: Classify HMI action events, service-panel endpoints and plant-control actions as control attempts.
Render control-attempt rows with a warning accent and badge in the Ops events table.
Keep normal HMI page-view events unmarked.
security_notes: The highlight is read-only presentation logic in the protected Ops backend.
No new public HMI endpoint, control path or authentication behavior is introduced.

title: Widescreen-safe Ops backend layout
summary: Lets the protected Ops backend use the full available width on normal displays while capping content at a 16:9 viewport ratio on ultrawide screens.
changes: Remove the old fixed 1280px Ops shell cap.
Let the Ops shell fill the viewport on normal displays.
Cap the Ops shell to a 16:9 viewport-derived width on widescreen layouts.
security_notes: The change affects only protected Ops presentation and does not expose new endpoints or data.
Tables remain horizontally scrollable as a fallback for narrow screens.

title: Full-width inverter service controls
summary: Moves the long inverter block-control section below the first four service cards so the protected service portal stays readable.
changes: Keep the overview, alarms, production and history service cards in a balanced four-card grid.
Render inverter block controls in a separate full-width panel below the compact cards.
Add regression coverage for the full-width inverter-control container.
security_notes: The layout change is presentation-only and does not add control endpoints or broaden HMI privileges.
The controls remain part of the honeypot lure surface and continue to use the existing service-session protections.

title: Service portal logout
summary: Adds an explicit logout action to the attacker-facing service portal while keeping session changes CSRF-protected and observable.
changes: Add a POST-only /service/logout action guarded by the service-panel CSRF token.
Clear the server-side service session and delete the service_session cookie after logout.
Render a Log Out button only when the service portal session is authenticated.
security_notes: Logout is POST-only to avoid link-prefetch or scanner-triggered session destruction.
The action affects only honeypot service sessions, not the protected Ops backend.

title: Production Docker defaults and local debug mode
summary: Simplifies production Docker exposure by fixing internal container ports, keeping only the HMI host port configurable, and replacing the exposure flag with local debug mode.
changes: Keep container-internal HMI, Modbus and Ops ports fixed while mapping only HONEYPOT_PUBLISHED_HMI_PORT on the host side.
Remove EXPOSED_RESEARCH_ENABLED and treat production exposure as the normal runtime.
Add HONEYPOT_LOCAL_DEBUG for explicit local lab or debug runs.
security_notes: The exposed Docker path no longer depends on a safety flag that can be misread; debug-only relaxations require an explicit local-debug opt-in.
Publishing the HMI on port 80 remains an operator mapping choice; Ops stays loopback unless deliberately changed.

title: Configurable service-login lure
summary: Moves the attacker-facing service-login lure credentials into protected Ops settings and changes the default lure to admin / sunshine.
changes: Use admin / sunshine as the default service-login lure credentials.
Expose editable service-login username and password fields in the protected Ops settings page.
Resolve HMI service-login success checks from persisted Ops settings while keeping brute-force logging unchanged.
security_notes: The service-login credential is an intentional honeypot lure and must not be reused for Ops, SSH, Caddy or other real access paths.
The lure password is stored and displayed in cleartext only inside the protected Ops backend.

title: Service-login robots lure
summary: Adds a public robots.txt hint that excludes the HMI service-login path to make the honeypot login surface more discoverable to scanners.
changes: Expose /robots.txt on the attacker-facing HMI surface.
List /service/login as disallowed while keeping the service-login route unchanged.
Keep robots.txt requests quiet so they do not create sessions or source activity events.
security_notes: robots.txt is intentionally a lure, not an access-control mechanism.
The file reveals only an existing honeypot path and does not reference the protected Ops backend.

title: DB-IP Lite GeoIP auto-update
summary: Automates Country and ASN MMDB retrieval for the protected source overview while preserving CC-BY attribution requirements.
changes: Add a fixed-URL DB-IP Lite updater for Country and ASN MMDB files.
Run the updater during Docker Compose startup so data/geoip is populated without manual downloads.
Write GeoIP metadata and render DB-IP CC-BY attribution in the protected Ops UI.
security_notes: The updater is limited to official DB-IP Lite HTTPS download paths and is not a generic URL fetcher.
GeoIP download failures do not block honeypot startup; stale or absent data simply leaves enrichment incomplete.
DB-IP Lite data is credited as CC BY 4.0 wherever Ops pages may display enriched source information.

title: GeoIP country and ASN autodetect
summary: Improves GeoIP database discovery so country codes and ISP organizations populate when operator-provided MMDB files use common variant names.
changes: Auto-detect Country MMDB files such as GeoLite2-Country and dbip-country-lite from the GeoIP mount.
Auto-detect ASN or ISP MMDB files with variant filenames in the GeoIP mount instead of requiring exact names.
Add generic Country-MMDB parsing for nested iso_code records.
security_notes: GeoIP databases are still local files only; the app performs no automatic downloads.
rDNS remains fallback-only after static maps and MMDB lookups.

title: ASN MMDB enrichment mount
summary: Adds a read-only GeoIP data mount and broader ASN-MMDB parsing so the protected source overview can show real network organizations.
changes: Mount ./data/geoip into the container at /app/data/geoip as read-only storage for operator-provided MMDB files.
Support MaxMind GeoLite2-ASN and generic ASN-MMDB schemas when resolving ISP/source organization names.
Keep rDNS as a fallback only when no ASN database result is available.
security_notes: ASN databases are local files only; the app does not download third-party data or embed licensed databases in the image.
The GeoIP bind mount is read-only inside the container.

title: Single production Compose path
summary: Simplifies deployment to one production Docker Compose service that starts with docker compose up without extra profiles or environment-file parameters.
changes: Remove the separate honeypot-exposed and honeypot-sweep Compose profile services.
Make docker compose up build the production honeypot with HMI and Modbus published by default.
Keep the Ops backend published on host-loopback by default while allowing OPS_PUBLISHED_HOST overrides for VPN, tunnel or reverse-proxy setups.
security_notes: The app still binds internally to the Docker network for future proxy/tunnel services, while host-side Ops exposure defaults to 127.0.0.1.
Opening OPS_PUBLISHED_HOST beyond loopback requires an explicit operator decision and should be paired with auth, firewalling or private access.

title: Source ISP fallback
summary: Keeps the protected source overview useful when no ASN database is configured by deriving a compact ISP hint from rDNS.
changes: Use ASN-MMDB data as the authoritative ISP source when configured.
Fall back to the rDNS parent domain for public IPs when ASN data is unavailable.
Add regression coverage for rDNS-derived ISP values and timeout handling.
security_notes: The fallback uses only already-enabled rDNS lookup data and does not add a new external HTTP enrichment service.

title: Sortable source activity
summary: Adds protected Ops source-table sorting so operators can quickly find the busiest or most recently active IPs.
changes: Add allowlisted sort and direction parameters to the protected /sources page.
Make source table headers clickable while preserving the selected row limit.
Add regression coverage for event-count sorting and invalid sort-parameter fallback.
security_notes: Sort parameters are normalized through a fixed allowlist and never used as raw SQL or unchecked field names.

title: Initial exposed-research release
summary: Marks the first V1 release after external HMI, Ops, Caddy and Modbus validation passed on the deployed target.
changes: Promote the project package and protected Ops version log to V1.0.0.
Record the deployed acceptance state for HMI pages, Ops backend authentication, Caddy security headers and public Modbus read access.
Carry forward the quiet HEAD probes, readable inverter layout and trusted-proxy source-IP handling as release gates.
security_notes: Public HMI and Modbus exposure are intentional honeypot surfaces; the Ops backend must remain protected by reverse-proxy authentication or a private access path.
The deployment uses HTTPS security headers at Caddy and forwards source IPs only through configured trusted proxies.

title: Readable inverter fleet layout
summary: Relaxes the /inverters page layout so block status, telemetry and alarm context stay readable without clipped text.
changes: Move the inverter comparison table onto a full-width HMI panel instead of squeezing it beside the alarm panel.
Widen the operational columns and render state values as bounded chips so status text stays inside its cell.
Add Playwright coverage for desktop and mobile overflow behavior on the inverter fleet page.
security_notes: Clear HMI telemetry reduces operator ambiguity during attacker testing and keeps honeypot observations easier to interpret.

title: Quiet HMI HEAD probes
summary: Handles normal HEAD probes on HMI read-only routes without creating internal-error events or session cookies.
changes: Add explicit HEAD handlers for the HMI healthcheck, overview, single-line, inverter, weather, meter, alarm, trend and service-login routes.
Keep HEAD probes quiet so they do not create page-view sessions or high-severity internal-error events.
Add regression coverage for HEAD /healthz, read-only HMI HEAD routes and disabled service-login behavior.
security_notes: Scanner and monitor HEAD probes now receive minimal status-only responses instead of triggering framework-style error paths.

title: Quiet HMI healthcheck endpoint
summary: Moves the container HMI healthcheck away from /overview so local probes no longer pollute attacker source statistics.
changes: Add a minimal /healthz endpoint on the HMI surface that returns status without creating sessions or events.
Update the Docker healthcheck to use /healthz while keeping the Modbus socket probe.
Add regression coverage that /healthz does not write page-view events.
security_notes: The public health endpoint intentionally exposes only a generic ok status and avoids leaking plant telemetry or observer state.

title: Trusted proxy source IP handling
summary: Adds guarded X-Forwarded-For handling so HMI and Ops events retain real client IPs behind a trusted Caddy proxy.
changes: Add FORWARDED_HEADER_ENABLED and TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS runtime settings.
Resolve HMI, service-login and Ops audit event source IPs through X-Forwarded-For only when the direct peer is trusted.
Add regression coverage for trusted proxy use, spoofed header rejection and backend audit events.
security_notes: Forwarded headers remain disabled by default and wildcard trusted-proxy CIDRs are rejected to prevent client-controlled source-IP spoofing.

title: Consistent HMI page width
summary: Aligns all attacker-facing HMI pages to the same outer shell width so the UI no longer changes width between pages.
changes: Use one shared 1440px shell width across overview, single-line, inverter, weather, meter, alarm, trend, service-login, service-panel and error pages.
Keep smaller page internals such as login forms constrained while the masthead and navigation stay aligned.
Add a regression test that renders all HMI page classes and checks the shared shell-width rule.
security_notes: This is a presentation-only hardening fix; it does not expose new endpoints or alter authentication behavior.

title: Service-login navigation placement
summary: Moves the service-login lure into the normal HMI navigation button group and removes the prominent overview card.
changes: Add Service Login to the same navigation group as Overview, Weather, Meter, Alarms and Trends.
Remove the Service Access metric card from /overview.
Keep the service-login link visible even when the service-login endpoint returns the quiet disabled page.
security_notes: The navigation item points only at the honeypot HMI login path and does not expose the protected Ops backend.

title: Overview service-login lure
summary: Adds a persistent Service Access card on the HMI overview that links attackers to the service-login path.
changes: Show the Service Access card on /overview regardless of service-login enablement.
Style the login link like the existing HMI buttons while keeping it inside the normal metric-card layout.
Keep disabled service-login behavior unchanged behind the link.
security_notes: The card exposes only the honeypot HMI login path and does not link to the protected Ops backend.
If service login is disabled for a deployment, the lure remains visible while /service/login still returns the quiet 403 page.

title: Backend version log
summary: Adds a protected Ops backend page that lists implemented features and fixes by version.
changes: Expose a readable version history in the Ops backend.
Use structured release entries with version, date, category, summary and affected areas.
Keep the first documented baseline below v1.0 while pre-exposure work is still active.
security_notes: The version log is only reachable through the protected Ops backend surface.

title: Credential campaign aggregation
summary: Aggregates service-login brute-force campaigns and stores All-Time and per-campaign credential counters.
changes: Sample the first service-login failures and aggregate later attempts into campaign summaries.
Store All-Time Top 100 usernames and cleartext passwords in the protected backend.
Support full CSV export for aggregated username and password counters.
Cap unique All-Time passwords at one million while continuing to count known values.
security_notes: Cleartext attempted passwords are kept out of normal auth events and stored only in dedicated credential tables.
Credential export remains an Ops backend function and must not be exposed on the public honeypot port.

title: Interactive inverter disconnects
summary: Adds visible QDC and QAC controls for inverter and PV field disconnect workflows.
changes: Expose disconnect switches in the single-line view.
Reflect disconnect state in simulated energy output.
Map related control functions through Modbus registers.
security_notes: Unauthenticated switch clicks are logged and redirected to the service-login flow.

title: Single-line energy-flow view
summary: Introduces a clearer interactive single-line diagram for park topology and energy flow.
changes: Separate DC-side PV field paths from AC-side inverter output paths.
Use established electrical symbols for inverter, breaker and grid presentation.
Relax diagram layout to avoid crowded labels and oversized arrows.
security_notes: Control affordances are visible to attackers, while real actions still require the service path.

title: Historical generation simulation
summary: Seeds plausible 30-day generation history so a fresh honeypot looks operational.
changes: Generate minute-level plant output from solar position and weather inputs.
Use historical weather or plausible fallback cloud-cover patterns.
Expose production trends and daily energy bars in the HMI.
security_notes: Historical data is synthetic and does not reveal real plant telemetry.

title: Ops settings and source enrichment
summary: Moves backend runtime settings into the protected Ops UI and enriches source IP overview rows.
changes: Persist backend settings in SQLite instead of growing the environment file.
Add toggles for source IP country, rDNS and ISP enrichment.
Add a protected action for deleting synthetic plant history.
security_notes: rDNS remains opt-in because it creates outbound DNS activity.

title: Dedicated Ops backend
summary: Adds an internal backend surface for observing attacker activity separately from the honeypot UI.
changes: Run the Ops backend on a separate port from the exposed HMI honeypot.
Show events, alerts, sources and runtime summary views.
Keep the backend suitable for VPN, tunnel or private-network access.
security_notes: The Ops backend is a sensitive observer surface and should not share the public honeypot ingress.
